# Muxy Hypeline for Unity

> Hypeline connects a Unity game to its live audience on Twitch: viewers trigger game actions and vote in polls through a Twitch extension, and the game shows each action as it happens.

The Unity package is installed from a Git URL in Unity Package Manager. A broadcaster signs in from inside the game with a short code, and the game receives viewer actions over a WebSocket connection.

## Docs

- [Getting-started guide](https://muxy.github.io/hypeline-unity/): installation, scene setup, the first viewer action, Twitch sign-in, polls, the C# API and troubleshooting. One static HTML page.
- [Hypeline for coding agents](https://muxy.github.io/hypeline-unity/agents.md): what an agent can do with one approval from the developer. Get access to the developer portal, register a Game ID, set up and check a scene from a JSON job file without the Unity Editor UI, and test the game in the sandbox with a test viewer.
- [Install prompt](https://muxy.github.io/hypeline-unity/prompts/install-hypeline.md): the instructions a developer gives a coding agent to carry out the guide and report what was verified.

## Examples

- [HypelineActionDemo.cs](https://muxy.github.io/hypeline-unity/examples/HypelineActionDemo.cs): a viewer-action handler used with the prefabs.
- [HypelineCodeDemo.cs](https://muxy.github.io/hypeline-unity/examples/HypelineCodeDemo.cs): a complete integration in C# without the prefabs.
